note: Expert and community consensus, gathered from FPL analysis sites and the official Scout. Prices and ownership here are as reported at research time and are only for context -- the app always matches players by name and uses live price/ownership from the API. Tiers are what actually drive selection.

players.name: Haaland
players.reason: Near-unanimous must-have and the consensus GW1 captain. Highest-projected player on the board, opening at home to Bournemouth, and already the most-owned player in the game at around 71-74%. At this ownership the armband isn't a differential call, it's the default -- not owning him is itself the active bet, and one you have to be right about.

players.name: B.Fernandes
players.reason: The safest premium midfielder on the board and the most-cited captaincy alternative when Haaland's matchup is awkward. On penalties and set pieces, and a nailed-on starter who plays essentially every minute -- the volume is what makes the underlying numbers bankable rather than streaky.

players.name: Raya
players.reason: Top-ranked goalkeeper and the only defensive player above 30% ownership, riding the same soft opening Arsenal fixture that pushes their defenders up the board.

players.name: Gabriel
players.reason: Leads the defender rankings. With Saliba out he's the primary route into an Arsenal defence with a soft opener, and carries a genuine aerial goal threat from set pieces on top of the clean-sheet case.

players.name: Semenyo
players.reason: Finished second among all midfielders last season on 202 points, and is priced well below the premium bracket. Widely flagged as the standout mid-price attacking midfielder.

players.name: Joao Pedro
players.reason: One of the two most-backed mid-price picks in preseason drafts -- the consensus way to free up budget for a Haaland-led attack without weakening it.

players.name: Szoboszlai
players.reason: The other most-backed mid-price pick. Set-piece involvement and a starting role make him the popular enabler in preseason drafts.

players.name: Calvert-Lewin
players.reason: Repeatedly named the standout value forward: completely nailed, expected to take penalties, and produced 16 attacking returns last season at a budget price.

players.name: Guehi
players.reason: The standout defensive value pick at around 26% ownership, with attacking output (xGI per 90) that is elite for a defender in this price bracket -- so the case isn't clean sheets alone.

players.name: White
players.reason: Ranked among the top two defenders on the same soft Arsenal opener, and cheaper than the more popular route into that defence.

players.name: Calafiori
players.reason: Just behind the leading Arsenal defenders in the rankings, sharing the same favourable opening fixture.

players.name: Saliba
players.reason: Out injured. Expert coverage explicitly routes around him to Gabriel and the other Arsenal defenders.
